terms_summary: BMG and Concord will combine under the BMG name, owned about 67% by Bertelsmann and about 33% by affiliates of Great Mountain Partners, which will also receive a one-time cash payment of $1.16 billion. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions, and is expected to close in the second half of 2026.

CVC Capital Partners, via its CVC Capital Partners IX fund, will acquire a majority stake in DistroKid, with Insight Partners retaining a significant minority stake. The deal is expected to close in Q3 2026, subject to customary closing conditions; terms were not disclosed.

Primary Wave acquired Kobalt's worldwide operations, owned copyright catalog and digital collection society amra from Francisco Partners, with an investment from Brookfield. A definitive agreement was reached in March 2026 and the deal closed on July 7, 2026 after regulatory approval; Kobalt will continue to operate as a standalone company under CEO Laurent Hubert.

Avex Music Group acquired producer-writer Infamous's catalog as its first purchase under a new catalog initiative supported by City National Bank. Financial details of the Infamous purchase were not disclosed; the initial $100 million commitment is the first phase of a broader catalog business.

Concord Cadence, a Concord subsidiary, will acquire the London-listed Round Hill Music Royalty Fund through a board-recommended offer of $1.15 per share, a 67.3% premium to the closing price on Thursday (September 7). The article gives no closing timeline.

Blackstone made a rival proposal of $1.24 per share in cash, topping Concord's $1.16 per share offer that the board accepted on April 18. The board said it would be minded to recommend Blackstone's proposal if a firm offer is announced, and it is giving Blackstone due diligence access. The Concord offer remains the recommended one until then.

Sony Music Publishing has acquired Hipgnosis Songs Group, formerly Big Deal Music, from Blackstone's Recognition Music Group, including about 4,400 copyrights and the Words & Music US publishing admin business. Financial terms and closing timing were not disclosed.

Britney Spears sold the rights to her music catalog to publisher Primary Wave, according to an anonymous source who said the deal was for approximately $200 million. Neither Spears' representative nor Primary Wave had commented, and no closing timing or structure was disclosed.
Pophouse Entertainment completed a transaction to become majority owner of the music interests of Tina Turner's catalogue, alongside BMG and the Tina Turner Estate. Terms were not disclosed.

Litmus Music acquired a portfolio of compositions, including select music publishing copyrights, covering hundreds of songs and numerous multi-platinum hits. Capital was invested by Carlyle Global Credit from its Credit Opportunities strategy; price and closing timing were not disclosed.

CVC Capital Partners signed a definitive agreement to make a majority investment in DistroKid through its CVC Capital Partners IX fund, with Insight Partners keeping a significant minority stake. Terms were undisclosed; the deal is expected to close in the third quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.
